title: Grade 10 Science — Electricity & Magnetic Effects of Current
description: Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Electric Current practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: The SI unit of electric charge is:
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in Coulombs (C). One coulomb is the charge carried by 6.24 × 10¹⁸ electrons. Ampere is the unit of current, not charge.

questions.question: Applying Ohm's law: if voltage across a resistor is 12 V and resistance is 4 Ω, the current flowing through it is:
questions.explanation: I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A. Ohm's law states V = IR, so current I = V ÷ R.

questions.question: When two resistors are connected in series, the total resistance is:
questions.explanation: In a series connection, resistors are added directly. Total resistance Rs = R₁ + R₂. The equivalent resistance is always greater than the largest individual resistance.

questions.question: The component used to vary the resistance in a circuit is called a:
questions.explanation: A rheostat (variable resistor) is used to continuously vary the resistance in a circuit, thereby controlling the current flow.

questions.question: Two resistors of 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
The power dissipated in a circuit with voltage 220 V and current 5 A is:
questions.explanation: P = V × I = 220 × 5 = 1100 W. This is the electrical power consumed by the device.

questions.question: The commercial unit of electrical energy used in households is:
questions.explanation: 1 kWh is the energy consumed when a device of 1000 W runs for 1 hour. This unit is used for electricity bills. 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

questions.question: A 100 W bulb is used for 2 hours and a 60 W bulb is used for 4 hours. Which consumes more electrical energy?
questions.explanation: Energy = Power × Time. 100 W × 2 h = 200 Wh. 60 W × 4 h = 240 Wh. The 60 W bulb consumes 240 Wh > 200 Wh.

questions.question: A device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is called a:
questions.explanation: An electric generator (dynamo) converts mechanical energy into electrical energy through electromagnetic induction. A motor does the opposite.

questions.question: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid carrying current is:
questions.explanation: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform (constant in magnitude and direction) along the axis. This makes solenoids useful for creating uniform magnetic fields.

questions.question: If the direction of current in a conductor placed in a magnetic field is reversed, the force on it will:
questions.explanation: By Fleming's Left Hand Rule, force F = BIL. If I (current) reverses, the force F reverses direction. Reversing the magnetic field would also reverse the force.

questions.question: Fleming's Left Hand Rule is used to determine the direction of:
options: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
Magnetic field around a straight conductor
questions.explanation: Fleming's Left Hand Rule (for Motors): thumb = motion (force), index = field, middle finger = current. It gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

questions.question: A DC electric motor converts:
questions.explanation: An electric motor uses the magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor to rotate a coil, converting electrical energy into mechanical (kinetic) energy.

questions.question: A transformer has 200 turns in the primary coil and 400 turns in the secondary. If primary voltage is 100 V, the secondary voltage is:
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np → Vs = (400/200) × 100 = 200 V. This is a step-up transformer as Ns > Np.

questions.question: AC is preferred over DC for long-distance power transmission because:
options: AC voltage can be stepped up using transformers, reducing energy losses
AC does not cause heating of wires
questions.explanation: Transformers work only on AC. By stepping up voltage (and reducing current), power loss P = I²R in transmission lines is greatly reduced. DC cannot be easily transformed.
